scope_statement: CI Score gauges best-practice adherence on CI speed and gate hygiene: a straightforward pass/fail rubric of best-practice checks computed from a repo's workflow configuration.
scope_note: The score reads CONFIGURATION FACTS a maintainer can verify in their own YAML in seconds. The measured wall-clock report renders beside it and enriches check evidence; measured magnitudes never gate a score in v1. Security stays out of v1 except SHA pinning (owner-named); runner-minute efficiency is reported alongside, not scored.

formula.score: round_half_up(100 * checks_passed / checks_applicable) - not_applicable leaves the denominator
formula.rounding: ROUND HALF UP - floor(x + 0.5). Python's round() is banker's rounding; any reimplementation must agree.

rules.config_facts_only: Every check is a YAML/configuration FACT (a thing present or absent in the repo's own files), never a measured magnitude, occurrence ratio, or attribution. A maintainer must be able to self-verify any state in under a minute against their own workflows. This is the v1-basic reset (decision_log OD-CS15): the magnitude-gated rubric generated wrongful-deduction bugs faster than review removed them, and a grade nobody can debug fails both the maintainer and us.
rules.evidence_display_only: Where the measured pipeline has evidence for a failed check (e.g. the uncached install's observed cost on the gating job), the card MAY display it under the check. Display only - it never changes a state.
rules.purity: the scorer is a pure function of (findings.json minus the stamp, this spec.json): no network, no clock, no LLM. Same inputs, byte-identical stamp.

bands_note: Suffix ranges are PINNED, not computed. The A band is 16 points wide and does not divide evenly into three, so an implementer who divides by three gets A- 85-90 while this spec says A- 85-89 - a repo scoring 90 would be published as 'A-' by one implementation and 'A' by another. All bounds are inclusive. F is never suffixed (there is no F+ / F-), matching the convention every reader already holds.

refusals.human_reason: No score: no GitHub Actions workflow files were found, so there is nothing to check.
No score: this document does not carry a complete practice-facts stamp for this spec version - re-run the skill to score this repo. This is a data-vintage limit, not a finding against the repo.
refusals.trigger: practice_facts is absent, or does not cover every check in this spec's registry (a partial stamp must never publish a score computed from the subset)

refusals.human_reason: Not scored: this repository's workflows show no build or test activity - what is visible is automation (bots, releases, triage), not the project's CI.
refusals.trigger: workflows exist (scanned_workflows > 0) but NONE do project build or test: no TEST signal (a test-like job id/name, OR a test-runner command in a step - pytest/go test/npm test/cargo test/rspec/... - so a real test-only repo whose job is named `ci` still scores), no BUILD signal (build tool / build-or-lint job / build command / build action), and no dependency-install COMMAND in any workflow. A setup-* action does NOT count (issue-triage bots use setup-node/setup-bun to run their scripts) and manifest presence does NOT count (an automation-only repo may carry a package.json its CI never installs). A repo that delegates its CI to a cross-repo reusable workflow is NEVER refused (invisible, not absent). Conservative: any one signal scores the repo. Added OD-CS20 after anthropics/claude-code, an npm package whose visible workflows are all issue-triage bots + release automation, graded a real-looking number off pure automation.

refusals_note: THREE refusals, all 'nothing to score honestly' shapes: no workflows at all; a document whose facts stamp is missing/incomplete for this spec version; or an automation-only repo whose workflows do no build or test (OD-CS20). Config facts need no run history, no branch-protection access, and no merge-queue calibration - every repo with REAL CI scores on a fresh run (owner directive, OD-CS15; OD-CS20 refuses only pure automation).

checks.label: Dependency caching
checks.fact: at least one workflow or local composite action configures dependency caching (a cache action - actions/cache incl. restore/save, rust-cache, buildjet - or a setup-* action's cache input). Caching housed in cross-repo reusable workflows is not visible; run the score in that repo.
checks.not_applicable_when: the repo shows NO dependency-install signal at all - no dependency manifest at the repo root (package.json / lockfiles / requirements*.txt / pyproject.toml / go.mod / Cargo.toml / build.gradle / pom.xml / *.csproj / mix.exs / build.sbt / Gemfile / composer.json / pubspec.yaml and the like), no dependency-install command in any workflow or composite step (pip / npm / pnpm / yarn / bun / poetry / uv / composer / bundle / gem / conda / mvn / gradle / dotnet / mix / cabal / stack with an install-style verb, or `go mod download` / `cargo fetch`), and no language setup action (actions/setup-node / setup-python / setup-java / setup-dotnet / setup-go / setup-ruby and the like) - and no cache is already configured; with nothing installed there is nothing to cache, so a missing cache is never a fail (OD-CS19). Any one of those three signals makes the check applicable. OR CI is delegated to cross-repo reusable workflows and no local caching is visible - a mechanism this fact cannot see is never failed

checks.label: Build caching
checks.fact: a build-tool cache is configured (turbo/nx/gradle/sccache/bazel remote or actions-cache-backed)
checks.not_applicable_when: no detectable build tool configuration in the repo tree (turbo.json / nx.json / settings.gradle(.kts) / .bazelrc)

checks.label: Shallow checkout
checks.fact: no checkout step on a PR-GATING workflow sets fetch-depth: 0 (structure-walked; comments never count; post-merge automation - a pull_request trigger whose types are only [closed], e.g. backport/changelog jobs - is exempt: it needs history and gates nobody)

checks.label: Test sharding / matrix
checks.fact: a test-like job (test/spec/e2e/integration/unit in its id or name) runs a matrix, or any job's matrix axis is shard-like (shard/chunk/split/partition)
checks.not_applicable_when: no test-like job (test/spec/e2e/integration/unit in an id or name) and no shard-like matrix axis exists in any parsed workflow - you cannot shard tests you do not have, so a missing shard is never a fail (OD-CS19); OR CI is delegated to cross-repo reusable workflows and no local test job is visible

checks.label: Change-scoped builds
checks.fact: CI scopes work to what changed: --filter=...[base], nx affected, --changed/--onlyChanged/--affected run modes, turbo-ignore, or a changed-files step (dorny/paths-filter, tj-actions/changed-files)
checks.not_applicable_when: no turbo/nx task graph is detected - gradle/bazel scoping is not checkable from workflow YAML and is never failed for a mechanism this fact cannot see

checks.label: Concurrency groups
checks.fact: at least one PR-triggered workflow declares a concurrency group (the config lever against self-stampede queue time)

checks.label: Superseded runs cancelled
checks.fact: at least one PR-triggered workflow sets concurrency with cancel-in-progress (true or a templated expression - conditional cancellation is the practice too; an explicit false is not)

checks.label: Path filters
checks.fact: at least one PR-triggered workflow scopes itself with paths / paths-ignore

checks.label: Job timeouts
checks.fact: workflow jobs set timeout-minutes (any usage; GitHub's default is 360 minutes)

checks.label: Scoped OIDC id-token
checks.fact: id-token: write is granted at job level, never workflow-wide (an explicit grant or a workflow-level permissions: write-all both count as workflow-wide)
checks.not_applicable_when: no workflow requests an OIDC id-token
checks.note: security-flavored; included under the owner's 'every best practice we have' directive

checks.label: Pinned action SHAs
checks.fact: at least 95% of remote action references are pinned to a full commit SHA, across workflow files AND local composite actions (first-party actions/* included - the pinning practice does not exempt them; the evidence always shows pinned-of-total). The threshold asks 'is pinning an adopted, automated practice?': >=95% admits Renovate-style stragglers (at most 1 in 20) while rejecting partial adoption, and is gaming-resistant - reaching it from a low base means actually pinning the fleet (OD-CS17)
checks.note: security-flavored; included by explicit owner direction (OD-CS15) despite D3's security-out-of-v1 scoping

stamp_schema._note: The shape the data pass stamps into findings.json as `ci_score`. Every surface renders FROM the stamp and never recomputes.
stamp_schema.value: int 0-100, or null on the single refusal

checks.label: string - the check's display label, copied from the registry
checks.evidence: string - the self-verifiable fact ('98 of 117 actions pinned', 'concurrency+cancel on ci.yml, e2e.yml'), never empty on fail
checks.measured_note: string or null - display-only enrichment from the measured pipeline
checks.files: list[str] - up to three files to look at, from the fact's evidence

v2_map._note: Punted wholesale by OD-CS15 - the v1-granular rubric (built through PR #225, superseded before publication). Everything here exists in git history and in the measured pipeline's stamps; none of it gates a v1 score.
punted: measured-magnitude fail gating (measured_only_fail, the two Doors, pole joins, pole_step_categories)
the 9-refusal lattice (merge-queue, evaluability floor, visibility caps)
v2_map.speed_effectiveness_checks: The decided path for measured speed into the composite (OD-CS16): size-fair effectiveness checks - retry-churn rate, self-inflicted queue time, shard balance, cache hit effectiveness - graded from the measured pipeline via the pole-anchored evidence machinery above. Raw gate-wait scoring (absolute or percentile) is REJECTED, not deferred: size-confounded (see OD-CS16).

decision_log.status: RESOLVED 2026-07-14 - executor recommendation under owner delegation ('come up with a recommendation and update the spec accordingly'); ratify alongside the Phase-3 pre-publication threshold review — SUPERSEDED for v0.1 by OD-CS15 (the measured rubric it governs is punted to the v2_map); its ratification review moves to the v2 design gate, not Phase 3.
decision_log.title: measured_only_fail makes 10 of the 13 checks unable to fail
decision_log.problem: The rule 'only sizing_basis == measured evidence can FAIL a check' is a hard product rule and its intent is right (never deduct on a public page from evidence we merely inferred). But the data pass stamps sizing_basis: 'measured' for only 13 detectors (OPT19/24/25/43/46/47/48/49/50/51/64/65/66), and those back only THREE of the 13 checks: ci.parallel.test-sharding (OPT24/25), ci.trigger.cancel-superseded (OPT46), and ci.trigger.queue-concurrency (OPT43). Every other check - INCLUDING both cache checks, the critical-path structural lever, and needless serialization, all of them majors - is capped at partial forever. Consequence: a repo with no dependency cache at all, a full-history checkout, and a 25%-of-gate structural lever cannot score below 50, and the card renders 'high confidence' beside it. The score is inflated by construction.
decision_log.why_it_was_missed: The product spec wrote the rule and then audited only two checks against it (path-filter and draft-gate, both correctly disclosed as dormant). The other eleven were never checked. The build plan then asserted the evidence-derivation block was 'executor-verified against the codebase'. It was not. The lesson: a rule ABOUT data is only as good as a census OF that data - a coverage claim needs a census, not a spot-check.

options.A: Broaden what counts as measured IN THE SCORER: sizing_basis == 'measured' OR the finding is sized off the measured critical path (carries an observed wall_clock_p50_s and joins to a pole). Scorer-only, no data-pass edit, no re-render of the six committed worked examples. Preserves the intent, because that evidence IS observed timing, not inference. Risk: a second, looser door into 'measured' - the definition must be tight and Phase-3 calibration must confirm it.
options.B: Fix the label at the source: widen _stamp_sizing_basis in the data pass. Most correct, but sizing_basis already gates savings totals and Tier-2 promotion, so it changes shipped report behavior and forces a re-render of all six committed reports.
options.C: Shrink the rubric to what can genuinely fail (3-5 checks). Honest, but breaks the owner-approved canonical description ('four-category, 13-check'), which is already in the website spec.
options.D: Ship as-is with the dormancy disclosed for all 10. Not recommended: a score where most checks cannot fail is close to vacuous, and 'high confidence' beside it is misleading.

decision_log.blocks: Blocked Phase 1 (the scorer) and everything downstream while OPEN. Resolved 2026-07-14 - Phase 1 may proceed; the resolution is ratified alongside the Phase-3 pre-publication threshold review.
decision_log.must_be_recorded_in: the product spec (maintained in the pre-public development archive), not only here - the rule lives there and the next reader must find the resolution beside it.
decision_log.resolution: The pole-anchored rule (formula.rules.measured_only_fail, Door 2): a fail test may read its magnitude from the drilled gating pole's observed step decomposition (steps[].p50_s / job_p50_s - observed over observed), from structural pole-anchored findings, or from measured chain membership - in addition to Door 1 (sizing_basis == 'measured'). Modeled constants remain banned from fail tests; an undrilled gate caps at partial. Scorer-only: no data-pass change, no re-render of the committed worked examples (poles already carry steps in every corpus). Second adversarial round refinements, same day: the join anchors on the finding's OWN workflow_file + affected_jobs (round 3 corrected round 2's claim that pr_critical_path_check was per-finding-resolved - it is the document's crown constant); structural findings qualify only from DRILLED poles; the Door-2 conjunction (deterministic YAML fact + observed magnitude in the check's pole_step_categories + the join) is explicit; step-name opacity is a disclosed lenient-direction limit.
decision_log.census_after_resolution: Checks able to FAIL: 7 immediately from fields that exist today (dependency-cache, build-cache, shallow-clone, no-repeated-setup, test-sharding, no-needless-serialization, critical-path-structure), +3 behind their named Phase-1 stamps (cancel-superseded: structured superseded counts; queue-concurrency: cause attribution; no-dead-required: YAML conditionality) = 10 of 13. path-filter and draft-gate stay dormant BY DESIGN (their occurrence evidence is deliberately not collected - new call shapes); real-gates-only is pass-or-partial on any published score by construction (its fail shape refuses the composite). All disclosed in the methodology.
decision_log.options_rejected: B (relabel more detectors 'measured' in the data pass) is not just riskier - the census shows it would be FALSE: 'direct'-sized magnitudes ARE heuristic constants (default_s), and relabeling them would let modeled numbers fail checks, the exact defamation vector the rule exists to block. C (shrink the rubric) breaks the owner-approved canonical description. D (ship inflated, disclosed) makes the score near-vacuous.

decision_log.title: v0.1 resets to a basic pass/fail best-practice rubric; the granular measured score is punted
owner_directives: The entire point of the product is to score any repo using the skill. We should fix this and score every repo.
We need to rethink this design. And punt on the complicated more granular score.
We need a basic version that just checks whether best practices are being followed and scores based on that. What you've designed is very comprehensive and overly complicated.
Make sure we include every best practice we have in the score but yes this is the right approach.
decision_log.context: The magnitude-gated rubric (OD-CS8, OD-CS13) was defamation-safety machinery that backfired: three adversarial rounds kept finding wrongful-deduction bugs CREATED by its complexity (the crown-join fiction, cross-workflow fail conjunction, cross-PR overlap attribution), a heavily-optimized control repo scored D+ for reasons only an expert dig could explain, and merge-queue repos could not score at all. Config-fact checks are self-verifiable, nearly bug-proof, need no run history or calibration, and score every repo.
decision_log.consequences: ONE refusal (no workflows). Merge queues score. Pinned SHAs enters by owner direction despite D3. The measured pipeline remains the report + display-only check evidence. OD-CS8/OD-CS13 machinery moves to the v2 map; their decision records stay for history. Amendment (same day): the registry covers all published best-practice pages - 12 checks; keep-advisory-checks-non-blocking is explicitly accounted for as not config-determinable (v2).

decision_log.status: DECIDED 2026-07-14 - owner ('Lets keep the score independent of speed'), after a three-review pressure test of the ranking
decision_log.title: The score stays independent of measured speed; speed is displayed beside it and enters the composite only as size-fair effectiveness checks in v2
reasoning: The emulated prior art does not score speed either: React Doctor grades code PATTERNS that correlate with performance (static scan, 0-100, fix-first), never runtime measurements - its virality was instant+actionable+shareable, and its most-criticized trait was formula opacity (which this spec inverts by being a public JSON file). A config-fact rubric IS the React Doctor shape.

Raw gate speed is size-confounded, measured on our own calibration set: score and merge-gate speed ANTI-correlate (Spearman ~ +0.5 across the 11 full-pipeline repos) because large monorepos adopt every practice and still run slow (test volume), while thin SDKs are fast because there is little to run. Scoring raw wait - even Lighthouse-style percentile curves - would publicly punish scale (sentry's 12-way-sharded pipeline eats a 'slow' label for being big). Lighthouse works for web pages because page speed is THE user outcome regardless of complexity; a CI gate's wait is not analogous.

The principled path for speed INTO the score exists and is deferred, not rejected: size-fair EFFECTIVENESS checks (retry-churn rate - the highest-scoring repos measured lowest; self-inflicted queue time; shard balance - sentry passes the sharding fact while its shard is the slowest measured gate; cache hit effectiveness). These measure pipeline engineering quality independent of repo size and ride the pole-anchored measured machinery already parked in the v2_map (OD-CS13).

Until then: adherence and speed are reported SIDE BY SIDE, never blended - the measured report renders beneath the card, and putting the measured wait ON the card is a pending display decision. This is the same reported-never-scored pattern as D4 (runner minutes).
decision_log.provenance: Pressure test 2026-07-14 (three adversarial reviews: ranking sanity, score-vs-measured, per-deduction fairness) - verdict: all deductions factually true, scores stand, no tuning; recorded in maintainers/ci-speedup/calibration/README.md.

decision_log.status: DECIDED 2026-07-14 - owner ('lets go with your recommendations for all except #2... we should just come up with a reasonable threshold'; on the >=95% proposal: '95% works, go ahead')
decision_log.title: The five pre-publication items ruled in one batch; pinned-action-shas passes at >=95% (the first post-freeze spec_version bump, v0.1.1)
rulings: Token-pass semantics: KEEP for v0.1, disclosed via the k-of-n evidence strings; gating-aware coverage is v2.

Pinning threshold: the check passes at >=95% of remote action references SHA-pinned (this bump). The rationale is the question the check actually asks - 'is pinning an adopted, automated practice?': >=95% admits Renovate-style stragglers (at most 1 in 20 references between update cycles) while rejecting partial adoption, and it is gaming-resistant (a repo below the bar reaches it only by actually pinning its fleet).
Waiver mechanism (.ci-score.yml): DEFER to v2 - the post-merge-automation exemption already absorbed the worst legitimate-full-history case.
Measured notes on published cards: a per-profile pre-publish checklist item at Phase 6, not a rubric rule.
Grade resolution: ACCEPTED for v0.1 - empirically closed by the 31-repo spread (0-100, four scoring 85, eight scoring 70-84, honest low scores).
(Mailto was already final - the 4x-confirmed owner directive; listed here only so the batch is complete.)
decision_log.never_tune_justification: Blast radius, censused over all 31 committed calibration findings docs BEFORE the change: exactly ONE repo flips - next-js at 146/147 = 99.3% pinned (67 -> 75). mastra at 101/120 = 84.2% stays a fail; every other pinning-failing repo sits below 80% pinned. The threshold was chosen from the practice-adoption rationale, not fitted to move rows - the census is the receipt that it could not have been (one row moved).

decision_log.title: The ci.trigger.draft-gate check is REMOVED from the registry (12 -> 11 checks; spec_version v0.1.1 -> v0.1.2)
decision_log.decision: Draft-PR gating is dropped from the CI Score. It is a contested COST PREFERENCE, not a consensus best practice - many teams push draft PRs precisely to get CI feedback before review, so gating on draft status trades feedback latency for runner spend in a direction reasonable teams disagree on.
rationale: Not a consensus practice: unlike every other check, draft gating optimizes one team's cost tradeoff against another team's feedback loop; there is no single correct answer to grade against.

Calibration evidence: in the B4 18-repo sweep the top-scoring exemplars (vitejs/vite 90, home-assistant/core 90) each failed ONLY this check - the rubric was docking otherwise-exemplary CI for declining a philosophy.

No best-practice page behind it: draft-gate is the one check with practice_slug null (no published /best-practices/github-actions/ page argues for it), so it fails the 'every check maps to a published practice' spine the registry otherwise holds to.
decision_log.timing: Pre-publication - nothing is public yet, so this is the cheapest possible moment for a rubric fix. spec_version bumps v0.1.1 -> v0.1.2.
decision_log.consequences: 11 checks. Every published best-practice page still maps to a check (draft-gate mapped to none, so the practice_coverage_note is unchanged). All committed corpus + synthetic stamps are recomputed under v0.1.2; the collected/ calibration receipts stay as their dated v0.1.1 snapshots. The draft-gate fact computation, its fix-table entry, and its methodology row are removed; the scorer arithmetic is unchanged (it iterates the registry, so a smaller registry simply scores over fewer checks).

decision_log.title: Two checks gain the applicability gate the rubric's own principle demands: dependency-cache is not_applicable only when the repo shows NO dependency-install signal at all (no manifest AND no inline install command), test-sharding is not_applicable without any test job (spec_version v0.1.2 -> v0.1.3)
decision_log.decision: The registry principle 'a check whose subject does not exist leaves the denominator; a mechanism this fact cannot see is never failed' already governs delegation, build-tool absence, and OIDC absence. Two content checks were not yet honouring it and could produce a FALSE FAIL: (1) ci.cache.dependency-cache failed a repo for not configuring a dependency cache even when the repo installs no dependencies at all - nothing is installed, so there is nothing to cache; (2) ci.parallel.test-sharding failed a repo for not sharding tests it does not have. Both now land not_applicable in those cases. For (1) the applicability signal is install-based, not file-based (see the round-6 retarget note in live_discovery): the check is applicable when ANY of three signals is present - a dependency manifest at the repo root, a dependency-install command in a step's run/script code, OR a language setup action (setup-node/python/java/dotnet/... - a general signal that does not depend on enumerating every ecosystem's install command); only a repo with NONE of the three is not_applicable.
decision_log.live_discovery: Found by dogfooding the public skills repo itself: its CI runs `pip install pytest pyyaml` and it was FAILED for not configuring a dependency cache. Round-6 dogfooding then exposed that a pure file-existence manifest gate was the wrong instrument on TWO counts: (a) it MISSED the motivating repo - the public skills repo actually carries a pyproject.toml (for pytest config, with dependencies=[]), so the file gate leaves it applicable, which is correct, but for the wrong reason and not because of the install it actually runs; and (b) a file-only gate would MASK real waste - a repo with no manifest file but a bare inline `pip install ...` in every run would go not_applicable, silently dropping a genuine fail from the denominator and INFLATING the grade. So the gate was retargeted to install-signal semantics: applicable when a manifest OR an inline dependency-install command exists; not_applicable only when the repo installs nothing at all. The skills repo is then applicable+fail on an honest basis (it installs deps and caches none - a real, two-step fix), and a manifest-less inline-install repo is applicable+fail (no masking).
gates: ci.cache.dependency-cache: before the pass/fail branch, test for an INSTALL SIGNAL - (i) a documented dependency-manifest file at the repo ROOT by file existence or glob (package.json + JS/TS lockfiles, requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.py/cfg, Pipfile(.lock), poetry.lock, uv.lock, go.mod/sum, Cargo.toml/lock, build.gradle(.kts), pom.xml, *.csproj/fsproj/vbproj, packages.config, mix.exs/lock, build.sbt, *.gemspec, cabal.project/*.cabal, stack.yaml, Package.swift, Gemfile(.lock), composer.json/lock, pubspec.yaml/lock), OR (ii) a dependency-install command in any workflow/composite step's run:/script: code (a structural-ish regex over the existing step_code collection: a package manager - pip/pipx/poetry/uv/npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/composer/bundle/gem/conda - with the install/ci/sync/add verb ADJACENT (only flags between, so `npm run ci` does NOT match), plus mvn/gradle/dotnet/mix/cabal/stack build-and-resolve commands, `go mod download`, and `cargo fetch`; shell comments are stripped before matching so a commented install never signals), OR (iii) a language SETUP action (actions/setup-node/python/java/dotnet/go/ruby/erlef/setup-beam/... - a general ecosystem signal, excluding non-runtime setup-* like docker/setup-buildx). If NONE of the three exists AND no cache is already configured -> not_applicable ('no dependency manifest and no dependency-install step detected; nothing to cache'). Cache hits present still PASS regardless of the signal; the existing reusable-delegation n/a is unchanged and takes precedence. The three-signal union (added after a review caught that a manifest+install-verb-only gate MASKED non-JS/Python/Go/Rust ecosystems - .NET/Elixir/Scala/monorepos - dropping their real dep-cache fails and inflating grades) keeps the n/a to genuinely dependency-free repos; a truly exotic ecosystem with no root manifest, no recognised install verb, and no setup action is the only disclosed residual n/a.

ci.parallel.test-sharding: if NO job in any parsed workflow has a test-like id or name (test/spec/e2e/integration/unit) AND no shard-like matrix axis (shard/chunk/split/partition) exists AND no remote reusables -> not_applicable ('no test-like job (test/spec/e2e/integration/unit) detected; nothing to shard'). A test job WITHOUT a matrix still FAILS (you have tests, shard them); the existing reusable-delegation n/a is unchanged and takes precedence.
decision_log.scorer_unchanged: ci_score.py arithmetic is untouched - both gates land another not_applicable state, which already leaves the denominator. Only practice_facts.py changed (an install-signal probe = manifest file existence/glob OR a step-code install regex OR a language setup action, and a job-shape probe); the check count stays 11.
decision_log.blast_radius: Computed by re-running the scorer over the 31-repo calibration set, never hand-derived. The test-sharding gate is determinable from committed data (workflow_job_graph carries every job id + name, so has_testish_job is computed directly; a committed sharding FAIL implies no shard-like matrix axis existed, so the gate genuinely fires when no test-like job is present). It moves exactly TWO rows, both small/atypical repos with no test-like job at all: anthropics/claude-code 44 -> 50 and coollabsio/coolify 22 -> 25 (value only). adobe/leonardo also has no test-like job but already scored 0/9 (0 passed), so it holds at 0. The dependency-cache install-signal gate fires on NO calibration repo: the three-signal union (manifest OR install command OR setup action) is strictly MORE applicable than both the file-only gate and the manifest+install-verb gate it succeeded, so it can only ever remove n/a cases, never add them, and every dep-cache-fail repo in the set - leonardo, claude-code, coolify, deepgram, discord.js, bun - carries a standard root manifest, runs an install step, and uses a setup action, so each stays applicable+fail; committed dep-cache facts are kept (signal presence for these rows is not recoverable from committed findings, but the direction is monotone so no row can flip to n/a). The six committed corpora each retain a test-like job (requests's sharding fail stays fail) and both frozen checkout controls hold at 82 (verified by re-running the collector on their committed trees; they pass dependency-cache on cache hits, so the retarget cannot touch them). Per-row receipt: maintainers/ci-score/calibration/dry-run-2026-07-28-v0.1.3.md.
decision_log.timing: Pre-publication, the same cheapest-moment argument as OD-CS18. spec_version bumps v0.1.2 -> v0.1.3.

decision_log.title: Automation-only repositories are NOT scored (third refusal added; part of the v0.1.3 bump)
decision_log.decision: A repository whose visible workflows do NO project build or test - only automation (bots, releases, triage) - is REFUSED, not scored. A technically-honest-but-absurd number on such a repo destroys trust in every other number; the owner chose refusal over a warning. New refusal reason_code `automation_only`, human reason 'Not scored: this repository's workflows show no build or test activity - what is visible is automation (bots, releases, triage), not the project's CI.' Home: refusals entry #3 + a scorer branch (compute_ci_score refuses when the collector sets doc.automation_only). ci_score.py arithmetic is otherwise unchanged; the check count stays 11.
decision_log.live_discovery: anthropics/claude-code scored a real-looking number (44, then 50 after OD-CS19's sharding gate) but its visible workflows are all issue-triage bots and release automation - the product's real CI is not in the repo. The number was technically honest and completely misleading.
decision_log.predicate: STRUCTURAL, from signals already computed on the parsed workflows. First, a repo that delegates its CI to a cross-repo reusable workflow is NEVER refused (a mechanism this fact cannot see is never failed - the module's standing rule). Otherwise refuse iff NONE of three project-work signals is present: (1) a TEST signal - a test-like job (test/spec/e2e/integration/unit in an id or name) OR a test-runner COMMAND in a run step (pytest / tox / go test / npm|yarn|pnpm test / bun test / jest / vitest / cargo test|nextest / rspec / phpunit / deno test / ctest / mix test / dotnet test / gradle|mvn ... test), because a real test-only repo commonly names its job `ci` and restores deps from a setup-* action rather than an inline install command - keying the test signal on the job NAME alone would false-refuse it; (2) a build signal - a build-tool/build-system config at the root (turbo/nx/gradle/bazel/Makefile/CMakeLists), a build-or-lint job name (build/compile/bundle/assemble/dist/package/lint/typecheck - NOT the bare word 'check', which names permission/status bots, and NOT deploy/release/publish, which are delivery), a build/lint command in a run step, or a container-build action; (3) a dependency-INSTALL COMMAND in a run step (npm ci, pip install, ...). A setup-* action does NOT count toward (3): issue-triage bots use setup-node/setup-bun to run their own scripts, so it is too weak to mean the project's CI installs its deps; manifest presence does NOT count either. Conservative by construction: ANY ONE signal scores the repo, so a small-but-real gate (a lint-only job, a single build job, a `pytest` step, `go test`) always scores - the design bias is toward scoring, never a false refusal.
decision_log.blast_radius: Verified, not assumed. Across the 31-repo calibration set, exactly THREE repos have no test-like job (computable from each committed findings.json's workflow_job_graph): anthropics/claude-code, coollabsio/coolify, adobe/leonardo - every other repo has a test job and scores. The committed findings predate this signal and carry no step-level data, so the build/install-command legs were resolved by re-collecting those three repos' workflows and running the predicate: (a) anthropics/claude-code REFUSES - every job is an issue/PR-management bot (its only apparent build/install signals are false: 'make' as an English word in a bot script, and setup-bun used by the triage bots), so its row becomes 'not scored'; (b) coollabsio/coolify SCORES - it has real build-push (docker image build) jobs; (c) adobe/leonardo SCORES - its pull_request ci.yml runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (a real install command). So the owner's initial three candidates resolve to ONE refusal on verification: only claude-code. The frozen no-test-job leg matches the committed snapshot for all three; the build/install legs are verified against current (2026-07-28) workflow shapes, whose automation-vs-CI character is stable. NET: one calibration row moves to 'not scored' (claude-code); coolify and leonardo keep their values; every scoring row is unchanged.
decision_log.scorer_unchanged: compute_ci_score gains one refusal branch (automation_only, ahead of facts_unavailable, behind no_workflow_yaml); the score arithmetic and the 11-check registry are untouched. The card and report render the refusal through the EXISTING refusal path (heading 'no score: <reason>', no grade, no recommendations, no disclosure) - verified.

changelog.change: Initial rubric: 4 categories, 13 scored checks, 5 informational entries, 9 refusal conditions (7 caps + merge_queue + low_evaluability). Encodes section 1 of the CI Score v0.1 build plan.
corrections: ci.parallel.test-sharding: legacy id corrected from OPT70 ('Scope the Build/Test to Only What Changed') to OPT23/OPT24/OPT25 (the actual sharding patterns).
ci.required.no-dead-required: OPT71 pin removed ('Expensive Non-Required Check on the Critical Path' is the inverse concept). Computed from required-check provenance fields instead.

ci.cache.dependency-cache: OPT1 pin removed ('Unnecessary Tool Install' is redundant work, not a cache defect). Third mis-binding of the same class; id-to-check bindings are now guarded by a golden manifest test against the catalog TITLES, not merely by an id-existence check.
Eight pinned ids had no detector at all and could never fire (OPT4/8/13/15/34/44/61/74); they are moved to dormant_rule_ids rather than silently dropped.
Refusal added: required_checks_unreadable - the common case on a repo you do not own (branch protection 404s), which previously surfaced as low_evaluability and read as the repo's fault.
Composite rounding pinned to ROUND HALF UP (Python's default round() is banker's rounding and gives 84 for 84.5, which straddles the B/A boundary).
Band suffix thirds pinned as explicit ranges (the A band is 16 wide and does not divide by 3).
Added the pass / not_applicable derivations and the refusal precedence rule, none of which existed.
Added the ci_score stamp schema (build plan section 1.4), which the first draft dropped - it is the contract the report card, the website pages, and the parity/recompute checks all consume.
known_gaps: OD-CS13: 10 of 13 checks could not fail under the original per-detector measured_only_fail rule. RESOLVED same day by the pole-anchored refinement (next entry; decision_log OD-CS13).

Three checks and one informational entry name a coverage_gap that Phase 1 must close before they can be computed at all: ci.trigger.cancel-superseded (OPT46 stamps its count only as prose, and the denominator is a different population), ci.trigger.queue-concurrency (OPT43 measures time-to-start, not queue; no cause attribution), ci.required.no-dead-required (no YAML trigger/filter data is emitted), and ci.gate.retry-tax (run_attempt is never stamped into findings.json).
refusals.merge_queue can only see OBSERVED merge_group runs; a configured-but-unused merge queue is not detected, because no declared-trigger data is emitted.

changelog.change: OD-CS13 resolved pre-publication: measured_only_fail refined to the two-door (pole-anchored) rule; fail_evidence declared per check against the fail_evidence_sources enum; open_decisions renamed decision_log with the resolution, census, and rejected options recorded.
corrections: The earlier framing 'this is a labeling gap, not a data gap' was WRONG for the cache/setup family: direct-sized findings genuinely carry heuristic default_s constants as their magnitude (census of _SIZING / _size_finding). The fix sources fail magnitudes from the drilled pole's observed step decomposition instead of relabeling modeled numbers.

changelog.change: Phase-1 build feedback: added the merge_queue_undeterminable refusal (9th; 7th cap) for old-vintage documents lacking both events_by_wf and workflow_triggers - the merge_queue coverage_gap mandated refuse-on-unavailable and the scorer needed a reason code for it; merge_queue's declared-trigger conjunct is now computable via the new scan.py workflow_triggers stamp; stamped checks gain an optional `note` field so by-design / blame-precise copy travels in the stamp the card renders from.

Phase-1 adversarial round (4 reviewers) corrections: the Door-2 join anchors on the finding's own workflow_file + affected_jobs (pr_critical_path_check is the document's crown CONSTANT, not a per-finding key - the round-2 sentence claiming otherwise was itself an un-censused evidence claim); OPT43 sibling windows come from the all-status slice (success-only windows structurally exonerate the cancelled siblings and turned self-inflicted queueing into a provider-congestion pass); determinable-absent merge-queue requires the DECLARED trigger stamp + a clean scan; types:-filtered PR triggers classify type_scoped (never unconditional -> never a false dead-required FAIL); attempt_stats carries workflows_missing and the retry-tax line renders only on complete coverage, same-population; composite arithmetic is exact (Fraction - float ties lost round-half-up on 4 reachable half-integer composites); an unobserved drilled-pole denominator caps at partial (never pass-by-silence); scoring failures stamp data_sources.ci_score_error; by-design notes only ever ride a pass; explicit cancel-in-progress false must be literally False.

OD-CS15 basic reset: 9 pass/fail config-fact checks, score = passed/applicable, ONE refusal, simplified stamp. The granular rubric (13 magnitude-gated checks, tiers, weights, 9 refusals, confidence) is punted to the v2 map before any publication. Bands and the purity/determinism/recompute architecture carry over unchanged. Amended same day per owner: 12 checks covering every published best-practice page (added change-scoped builds, concurrency groups, scoped id-token); keep-advisory-checks-non-blocking documented as not config-determinable (v2).

Post-reset adversarial round: _practice_facts rewritten as a YAML-STRUCTURE walk (raw-substring scanning produced false FAILs from comments, cross-step regex windows, and the 'sphinx contains nx' applicability bug, and false PASSes from tokens in comments). Facts now see local composite actions; dependency-caching recognizes cache-action families (rust-cache etc.) and actions/cache/restore+save; test-sharding recognizes e2e/spec/integration/unit jobs and shard-like matrix axes; change-scoped is n/a for gradle/bazel (undetectable mechanisms are never failed); draft-gate is n/a without PR workflows (merge-queue-only repos are not dinged); workflow-level write-all fails scoped-id-token; pinned-SHAs counts ALL remote references incl. first-party, across composite actions, with corrected wording. Second refusal added (facts_unavailable) so vintage/partial-stamp documents refuse with an honest reason and a partial stamp can never publish a subset score.

Persona round (scored-maintainer + Series-B CTO): PR-GATING replaces PR-triggered for the PR-path checks (types-only-[closed] post-merge automation like backport jobs is exempt - the maintainer persona's top grievance, and our own methodology example was the false positive); cross-repo reusable-workflow delegation lands not_applicable on the content checks, never fail (the CTO's uninstall event - 'never fail a mechanism this fact cannot see' now applies to every check); evidence strings count all offenders and never phrase a capped file list as exhaustive (mastra has six fetch-depth offenders, the card named three as if complete); pinning offender files rank third-party first; draft-gate evidence uses k-of-n framing. Owner-decision items recorded in pre_publication_requirements.

Phase-3 calibration recorded: 31-repo dry-run under blob 9d891b137f0b, zero rubric edits motivated (the calibration block is the receipt). OD-CS13's ratification venue moved to the v2 gate (its rubric is punted). The registry is now FROZEN for v0.1: any further change requires a spec_version bump — the pre-publication window closed with the calibration.

Owner directive (4th confirmation): dispute machinery is removed from every surface and never re-surfaced as a concern or requirement. The ONE feedback channel on score pages is the mailto ('contact us for issues/corrections'). The pre_publication_requirements item is rewritten accordingly.

OD-CS16 recorded: the score stays independent of measured speed (owner-decided after the ranking pressure test). Reasoning preserved in the decision log: React Doctor itself grades patterns not runtimes; raw gate speed is size-confounded (measured anti-correlation ~ +0.5 on our own calibration set); the v2 path is size-fair effectiveness checks (v2_map.speed_effectiveness_checks). Speed remains reported-never-scored beside the grade, the D4 pattern.

First post-freeze spec_version bump (OD-CS17): ci.security.pinned-action-shas passes at >=95% of remote action references SHA-pinned, replacing all-or-nothing. Owner-decided 2026-07-14 ('95% works, go ahead') with the practice-adoption rationale (admits Renovate-style stragglers, rejects partial adoption, gaming-resistant). Blast radius censused over all 31 committed calibration docs before the change: exactly one repo flips (next-js, 146/147 = 99.3%, 67 -> 75); mastra (101/120 = 84.2%) stays a fail and every other pinning-failing repo is below 80%. The same batch ruled the remaining pre_publication_requirements items DECIDED (token-pass kept+disclosed, waivers deferred to v2, measured-notes as a Phase-6 checklist item, grade resolution accepted); all committed stamps are recomputed under the new version.

Second post-freeze spec_version bump (OD-CS18): the ci.trigger.draft-gate check is REMOVED (12 -> 11 checks). Draft-PR gating is a contested cost preference, not a consensus best practice (many teams push draft PRs precisely to get CI feedback before review), the B4 18-repo sweep showed top-scoring exemplars (vitejs/vite 90, home-assistant/core 90) failing ONLY this check, and it is the one check with no published best-practice page behind it (practice_slug null). Pre-publication, the cheapest moment for a rubric fix. All committed corpus + synthetic stamps are recomputed under v0.1.2; the collected/ calibration receipts stay as their dated v0.1.1 snapshots (matched findings.json + report.md receipts kept coherent). Score movement, recomputed over the full 31-repo calibration table: every row shifts a few points because ~60% of the set was failing the removed check (promotions only, none demoted) - e.g. OneSignal-Flutter-SDK, requests, oven-sh/bun, cal.com, Infisical, nx and redpanda all rise, mastra/langfuse/grafana move 83 -> 82, deepgram holds, mastodon holds at 100. The complete per-row before/after (numeric) is in maintainers/ci-score/calibration/dry-run-2026-07-28-v0.1.2.md.

Third post-freeze spec_version bump (OD-CS19): two checks gain the applicability gate the rubric's own principle already demanded ('a mechanism this fact cannot see is never failed'). ci.cache.dependency-cache is not_applicable when the repo shows NO dependency-install signal at all - NONE of three signals: (i) a dependency manifest at the repo root (package.json + JS/TS lockfiles, requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.py/cfg, Pipfile(.lock), poetry.lock, uv.lock, go.mod/sum, Cargo.toml/lock, build.gradle(.kts), pom.xml, *.csproj/fsproj/vbproj, packages.config, mix.exs/lock, build.sbt, *.gemspec, cabal.project/*.cabal, stack.yaml, Package.swift, Gemfile(.lock), composer.json/lock, pubspec.yaml/lock), (ii) a dependency-install command in a step (pip/npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/poetry/uv/composer/bundle/gem/conda with an install-verb ADJACENT, plus mvn/gradle/dotnet/mix/cabal/stack build commands, `go mod download`/`cargo fetch`; shell comments stripped first), (iii) a language setup action (setup-node/python/java/dotnet/...) - and no cache is already configured; with nothing installed there is nothing to cache. The gate is install-signal, not file-only: round-6 dogfooding showed a pure file-existence gate both MISSED the motivating repo (the public skills repo carries a pyproject.toml, so a file gate leaves it applicable but for the wrong reason) and would MASK real waste (a manifest-less repo with a bare inline `pip install ...` would go n/a, dropping a genuine fail and inflating the grade); a later review caught that a manifest+install-verb-only gate still MASKED non-JS/Python/Go/Rust ecosystems (.NET/Elixir/Scala/monorepos), which the setup-action signal and the broadened manifest/verb lists close. Applicable when ANY of the three signals exists; not_applicable only when NONE. ci.parallel.test-sharding is not_applicable when no test-like job (test/spec/e2e/integration/unit) and no shard-like matrix axis exists anywhere - you cannot shard tests you do not have. A cache hit still PASSES regardless of the signal; a test job WITHOUT a matrix still FAILS. Scorer arithmetic unchanged (both gates land another not_applicable, which already leaves the denominator); check count stays 11. Blast radius, computed over the full 31-repo calibration table under v0.1.3 (the test-sharding gate is determinable from committed data via workflow_job_graph; the dependency-cache install-signal gate is strictly more applicable than the file-only gate it replaced, so it can only remove n/a cases and never add them - it fires on NO calibration repo, every dep-cache-fail row carrying both a standard manifest and an install step, so committed dep-cache facts are kept): TWO rows move, both small/atypical repos with no test-like job, from the sharding gate firing - anthropics/claude-code 44 -> 50 and coollabsio/coolify 22 -> 25 (value only); adobe/leonardo has no test job either but already scored 0 (0 passed) so it holds at 0. Every other row is unchanged. The six committed corpora each retain a test-like job (requests's sharding fail stays fail) and both frozen checkout controls hold at 82 (re-run on their committed trees; they pass dependency-cache on cache hits, so the retarget cannot touch them). Committed corpus + synthetic stamps re-stamped under v0.1.3 (spec_version field only; facts and scores unchanged, since each keeps a manifest and a test job); collected/ calibration receipts stay their dated snapshots. Per-row receipt: maintainers/ci-score/calibration/dry-run-2026-07-28-v0.1.3.md.

practice_coverage_note: Published /best-practices/github-actions/ page coverage (corrected 2026-07-29, OD-CS21 - two pages had shipped after this note was first written and were unaccounted): keep-advisory-checks-non-blocking has NO scored check (whether an advisory check blocks merges lives in branch-protection semantics, not workflow YAML, so no configuration fact can decide it honestly - deferred to v2 with the required-checks data); replace-fixed-sleeps-with-polling has NO scored check (fixed-sleep detection is step-content judgment, not a configuration fact a maintainer can verify in their own YAML in seconds - candidate for a future rubric revision); bound-job-timeouts IS scored (ci.hygiene.job-timeouts) but its practice_slug binding is null here because the page shipped after the v0.1.1 freeze - the report renderer supplies the link.
